test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 10 March, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: P alone can complete a piece of work in 10 days while Q alone can complete the same piece of work in 15 days. To complete the work in 4 days, R is hired by P and Q. How many days does R take to complete the work alone?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(10, 15, 4) = 60 units

Efficiency: P = 6, Q = 4, P + Q + R = 15

Efficiency of R = 15 − (6 + 4) = 5 units/day

Time for R alone = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 days

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P = 10 days

Time taken by Q = 15 days

Time taken by P + Q + R together = 4 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of P = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of P + Q + R = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of R = (Efficiency of P + Q + R) − (Efficiency of P + Efficiency of Q)

⇒ Efficiency of R = 15 − (6 + 4) = 5 units/day

⇒ Time taken by R alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of R

⇒ Time taken by R alone = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 days

**∴ The correct option is D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Relation of Time and Efficiency

Time taken to complete a work is inversely proportional to the efficiency of the worker. Time = 1 ÷ Efficiency (keeping work constant).

Combined Work Formula

If A, B, and C can do a work in x, y, and z days respectively, their combined 1-day work is (1/x + 1/y + 1/z).

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in the direct ratio of the amount of work done, which is also the ratio of efficiencies if they work for the same duration.</p
